name: Health Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public health data.

entries.title: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)
entries.description: The nation's premier system of health-related telephone surveys collecting state data on US residents' risk behaviors, chronic conditions, and use of preventive services.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
entries.attribution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, BRFSS
entries.notes: Annual survey data released as SAS transport and ASCII files with documentation.

entries.title: CDC Open Data Portal (data.cdc.gov)
entries.description: CDC's open data portal — hundreds of public health datasets (surveillance, vital statistics, vaccination, environmental health) with a SODA API.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
entries.notes: Socrata-based portal with a SODA API.

entries.title: FluView — CDC Influenza Surveillance
entries.description: CDC's weekly U.S. influenza surveillance report — outpatient illness, virologic, hospitalization, and mortality indicators for seasonal flu.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
entries.notes: Data via FluView Interactive and the API.

entries.title: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
entries.description: National survey data on the health and nutrition of adults and children in the United States, combining interviews with physical examinations and laboratory tests.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)
entries.attribution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics, NHANES
entries.notes:
Public data files and documentation are published at https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/Default.aspx (verified 2026-08-02).
Continuous NHANES has been conducted since 1999 with public-use data released in two-year cycles; the predecessor National Health Examination Survey began in 1959.

entries.title: National Vital Statistics System (NVSS)
entries.description: CDC/NCHS system for U.S. vital statistics data on births, deaths, fetal deaths, and related records, including mortality and natality statistics.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)

access.auth_note: Public-use files are open; restricted-use microdata requires an approved NCHS Research Data Center application.

entries.attribution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics, NVSS
entries.notes:
The NVSS homepage links to CDC WONDER, downloadable final data, restricted-use data, and documentation for major vital statistics products.
Mortality public-use documentation is published at https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/mortality_public_use_data.htm (verified 2026-08-02).
Much of the mortality and natality data here is queryable through CDC WONDER (catalog entry cdc-wonder); this entry covers the underlying system and its downloadable public-use files.

entries.title: PLACES: Local Data for Better Health
entries.description: Model-based small-area estimates of chronic disease measures, health behaviors, and prevention indicators for US counties, places, census tracts, and ZCTAs.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
entries.attribution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, PLACES
entries.notes: Downloadable datasets are served via the CDC open data portal (data.cdc.gov).

entries.title: WISQARS — Injury Statistics
entries.description: CDC injury statistics query system for fatal and nonfatal injury, violent death, and cost-of-injury data in the United States.
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
entries.attribution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, WISQARS
entries.notes: Issue source URL https://www.cdc.gov/injury/wisqars/ serves a CDC meta-refresh page to the live WISQARS application at https://wisqars.cdc.gov/.

entries.title: CDC WONDER
entries.description: CDC's Wide-ranging ONline Data for Epidemiologic Research — an integrated query system for dozens of public health datasets (mortality, natality, cancer, notifiable diseases, and environmental exposures).
entries.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
entries.attribution: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, CDC WONDER
entries.notes: Query-based access; sub-national counts are privacy-suppressed. The API uses an XML request format.

entries.title: CMS Data (Medicare & Medicaid)
entries.description: Claims-based utilization, spending, and provider data for Medicare and Medicaid.

entries.title: Eurostat Health Statistics Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU health statistics: health status and healthy life years, health determinants (European Health Interview Survey), health care resources, expenditure and activities, causes of death, and health and safety at work, harmonised across EU member states.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: Eurostat free re-use policy (data reuse authorised for commercial or non-commercial purposes provided the source is acknowledged; Commission Decision of 12 December 2011)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The page is "Database - Health - Eurostat", with "Selected datasets" and "Detailed datasets" tabs whose dataset tree loads by JavaScript and did not render in the headless session. Eurostat's catalogue table of contents (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/catalogue/toc/txt?lang=en) answered HTTP 200 and lists a "Health" folder (code hlth) with subfolders "Health status", "Health determinants", "Health care", "Causes of death" and "Health and safety at work", holding 496 datasets. The latest data update listed is 27.10.2026, and "Causes of death - deaths by country of residence and occurrence" (hlth_cd_aro) was last updated 23.09.2026. A JSON request for hlth_cd_aro through the dissemination API (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/) returned HTTP 200. The formats listed are Eurostat's usual download options and weren't checked one by one.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: Eurostat's "Copyright notice and free re-use of data" (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) says editorial content "is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence", and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged. The reuse policy of the European Commission is implemented by the Decision of 12 December 2011." Exceptions cover third-party material and data "identified as belonging to sources other than Eurostat" (non-commercial reuse only). The notice ties CC BY 4.0 to editorial content, and the data sentence names no licence, so this entry quotes the data reuse terms rather than labelling them CC-BY-4.0, as some sibling Eurostat entries do.

entries.title: OECD Health Statistics
entries.description: The OECD's cross-country database on health spending and health systems: health expenditure and financing (System of Health Accounts), health status, risk factors, healthcare human and provider resources, healthcare use, quality and outcomes, pharmaceutical markets, coverage and long-term care, for OECD members and selected partner countries.
entries.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

coverage.spatial: OECD member countries and selected partner economies

entries.license: unverified — OECD terms page (oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html) is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and could not be read
entries.attribution: OECD, OECD Health Statistics (OECD Data Explorer)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl; the Data Explorer is a JavaScript app and was read in headless Chromium). The issue's URL, https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/oecd-health-statistics.html, returned a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (HTTP 403) to curl, headless Chromium (new headless mode, 25-second wait) and WebFetch, so this entry points at the OECD Data Explorer, where OECD serves the data. With the Topic facet set to Health it reports "86 datasets found", grouped into "Health expenditure and financing" (5), "Health status" (16), "Risk factors for health" (7), "Healthcare human resources" (16), "Healthcare provider resources" (6), "Healthcare use" (10), "Healthcare quality and outcomes" (14), "Pharmaceutical market" (4), "Healthcare coverage" (1) and "Long-term care" (4). The SDMX API (https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/) answered HTTP 200 and lists these under agency OECD.ELS.HD, for example DSD_SHA@DF_SHA "Health expenditure and financing" and DSD_HEALTH_STAT@DF_LE "Life expectancy". I did not confirm that every OECD.ELS.HD dataflow belongs to the product OECD brands "OECD Health Statistics", and I did not see a latest release date. The formats are taken from the Data Explorer's usual download and API options and weren't tested.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. The Data Explorer's terms link goes to https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, which was blocked as above. Another vertical's entry (labor-almanac oecd-employment-labour-market) quotes those terms as allowing reuse of Data "for any purpose, even for commercial use" with credit. I could not read them this session, so no licence is asserted here.

entries.title: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO)
entries.description: The World Health Organization's portal for global health statistics — curated indicators on mortality, disease burden, health systems, and the determinants of health for WHO member states.
entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 with WHO additional terms (WHO data terms and conditions, data.who.int)
entries.attribution: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory
entries.notes:
Programmatic access via the GHO OData API (https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/).
Licence checked 2026-10-31: WHO's data terms (https://data.who.int/about/data/terms-and-conditions, repeated on data.who.int indicator pages) say "Unless specifically indicated otherwise, these Datasets are provided to you under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0), with the additional terms below" (attribution, no de-anonymisation or misrepresentation, arbitration, termination). The CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO licence recorded here earlier is WHO's licence for publications. The GHO pages themselves state no licence, and an older WHO data policy page (https://www.who.int/about/policies/publishing/data-policy/terms-and-conditions) still grants use only "for public health purposes"; that the GHO falls under the data.who.int terms is an inference a steward may want to confirm.

entries.title: WHO Mortality Database
entries.description: Global mortality data reported annually by WHO Member States from civil registration and vital statistics systems, with cause-of-death detail for comparative epidemiological studies.
entries.attribution: World Health Organization, WHO Mortality Database
entries.notes:
The WHO page states that the database is compiled from mortality data reported annually by Member States and that the visualization/export portal covers cause-of-death data from 1950 to date. The raw data section was last updated on 23 February 2026 when verified on 2026-08-03.
WHO states that no commercial use permission is implied for these transmitted data, and the database page does not identify a named license, so the license field is intentionally narrower than the WHO GHO catalog entry.
